title: Ian Hague, London College of Communication (UAL)
use_cases: Use when researching multisensory theory and materiality in graphic novels
Use when seeking information on Comics Forum conference history and leadership
Use when referencing academic experts in Interaction Design and Visual Communication at UAL
Use when identifying scholarship regarding the representation of violence and multiculturalism in sequential art
content: Dr Ian Hague is a Senior Lecturer and Year 3 Coordinator in Contextual and Theoretical Studies at London College of Communication (UAL), where he is based in the Interaction Design and Visual Communication Programme. His research looks at comics and graphic novels, and how they engage with questions of materiality and experience. Ian is the author of Comics and the Senses: A Multisensory Approach to Comics and Graphic Novels (Routledge 2014) as well as numerous shorter pieces, and the co-editor of Representing Multiculturalism in Comics and Graphic Novels (Routledge 2015), Contexts of Violence in Comics (Routledge 2019) and Representing Acts of Violence in Comics (Routledge 2019). In 2009, Ian founded Comics Forum, an annual conference on comics that runs as part of the Thought Bubble sequential art festival in Leeds. In 2011, he launched Comics Forum website, which publishes scholarship from a wide range of academics and thinkers on comics from around the world. Ian is also an experienced designer.
